answer: Unique endpoint binding assigns each identity a vertex in a public interaction graph and one non-transferable channel endpoint. Every action must carry a fresh challenge signed through that endpoint; duplicated agents sharing it collide on sequence numbers, so the copy reveals itself and both identities freeze. The attacker pays one live endpoint and a persistent haven slot per identity, each needing a separate hardware-key ceremony or paid relay lease. A duplicate leaves an ember in the relay log—a retained replay token costing one metered lease per alias and forfeited on detection.
